- Stratify land cover map by Forest Type and Deforestation Risk

Project Area Stratification

- Simple Random
- Every sampling unit (pixel) has an equal chance of being sampled.
- Advantages:
- Maximum potential sampling units (if sample size needs to be increased)
- Disadvantages:
- Difficult to locate in the field

- Simple Systematic
- Samples are at fixed distance and heading from each other
- Advantages:
- Easy to locate in the field
- Disadvantages:
- Fewer potential sampling units
- Confounding spatial patterns must be identified and stratified (eg. Terrain, Farmland)

- Clustered
- Cluster of samples generated around initial selected unit
- *Can be used with Simple Random or Simple Systematic
- Advantages:
- High confidence with interpretation data
- Disadvantages:
- Data within sampling group is correlated
- High LOE, time-intensive

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
- Useful Resources
- OpenMRV: Sampling design for estimation of area and map accuracy
- Basic Concepts
- Area proportions determines sample allocation
- Expected accuracy determines sample size*
- Balance between minimum accuracy requirements and LOE

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
- What it affects
- Larger: Estimated accuracy is closer to actual accuracy
- Smaller: Less effort, less time, less QAQC
- Considerations
- Larger samples won’t increase accuracy
- Stratification quality is critical
  - Modularity [easy to divide strata]
  - Representative of reality
- Increase sampling strategically if your initial assumptions result in inaccuracies

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| .reduceRegion | Uses a geometry to calculate from the input raster a statistic defined by a Reducer Useful to calculate area proportions |
| ee.Reducer | Defines a statistic for the .reduceRegion function |
| ee.Image.pixelArea() | Dynamically calculates the projection-defined area of each pixel of a raster, turning each pixel into the area in square meters Divide the resulting raster by 10000 to convert it to hectares Useful to calculate area proportions |
| .updateMask | Eliminating areas with another raster value mask from being sampled |
| .stratifiedSample | Accepts a list of sample sizes [Sample Size List] Accepts a list of raster values for the land cover map [Classified Map List] For each value of the raster listed in the Classified Map List, selects the number of pixels listed in the Sample Size List and creates a point at the center of the selected pixels. Recommended to assign a sample size larger than designed, then trim the samples by strata later |

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| .buffer | Transforms a point into a circular polygon Useful to create clustered samples Useful to detect spatially overlapping samples |
| .bounds | Transforms a circular polygon into a square polygon Useful to create square sampling plots |
| .iterate | Runs a iterative function that returns the results of the function to a first element (a List or FeatureCollection) Useful to check for overlaps iteratively between samples within a specified distance Computationally intensive and needs to be run in a separate step Less computationally intensive than running a .function with filters |
| .limit | Trims a FeatureCollection down to a specified size Useful within a function to trim a sample within a strata down to the desired sample size. |
